question: A man travels \(m\) feet due north at \(2\) minutes per mile. He returns due south to his starting point at \(2\) miles per minute. The average rate in miles per hour for the entire trip is:
solution:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Let \(d>0\) be the one-way distance measured in miles; its numerical value will cancel.

The outward pace is \(2\) minutes per mile, so that leg takes \(2d\) minutes. The return speed is \(2\) miles per minute, so the return takes \(d/2\) minutes. Hence
\[
\text{total distance}=2d\text{ miles},
\qquad
\text{total time}=2d+\frac d2=\frac{5d}{2}\text{ minutes}.
\]
Because \(d>0\), we may cancel it in the quotient:
\[
\text{average speed}
=\frac{2d}{5d/2}
=\frac45\text{ mile per minute}.
\]
There are \(60\) minutes in an hour, giving
\[
\frac45\cdot60=48\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
Thus the answer is choice B, independently of the value of \(m\).

nodes.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions , including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. nodes.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed. For example, if it took 7 hours to mow 4 lawns, then at that rate, how many lawns could be mowed in 35 hours? At what rate were lawns being mowed?
